pairs.question: Quibus hic pretiis porci veneunt sacres sinceri?
pairs.derivation: Menaechmus asks Cylindrus the price of sacrificial pigs; cook answers 'Nummis' (for coins). Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Responde mihi, adulescens:' preceding the interrogative. Stripped the inline verse number 290 that follows 'Nummis.' on the same line; what follows is Menaechmus' next utterance 'Nummum a me accipe'.

pairs.question: Est tibi nomen Menaechmo?
pairs.derivation: Within Messenio's interrogation, a clean yes/no interrogative ('Is your name Menaechmus?') genuinely answered 'Fateor' (I admit it). Dropped surrounding speaker labels MESS./MEN. and the adjacent further questions on the same line.

pairs.question: Esne tu Syracusanus?
pairs.derivation: Messenio asks 'Are you a Syracusan?'; Menaechmus answers 'Certo' (Certainly). Dropped speaker labels and the following 'MESS. Quid tu? SOS. Quippini?' on the same line.

pairs.question: Quot eras annos gnatus, quom te pater a patria avehit?
pairs.derivation: Messenio asks how old he was when his father took him from home; answer 'Septuennis' (seven). Answer window stops at the first full stop: cut the elaboration 'nam tunc dentes mihi cadebant primulum. neque patrem umquam postilla vidi' which follows. Stripped the inline verse number 1115. Dropped the speaker label MESS.

pairs.question: Vos tum patri filii quot eratis?
pairs.derivation: Messenio asks how many sons there were; answer 'two, as best I now recall'. Dropped the exclamatory framing 'Quid?' and the speaker labels MESS./MEN. Kept the full single-sentence reply.

pairs.question: Vter eratis, tun an ille, maior?
pairs.derivation: Messenio asks which of the two was older; answer 'both equally the same'. Dropped the speaker labels MESS./MEN.

pairs.question: Qui id potest?
pairs.derivation: Messenio asks how that is possible (that they were equal in age); answer 'we were both twins'. Dropped speaker labels MESS./MEN. and the following 'SOS. Di me servatum volunt' and the inline verse number 1120.

pairs.question: Uno nomine ambo eratis?
pairs.derivation: Messenio asks whether both had one name; answer 'Minime' (Not at all). Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Dic mihi:' that precedes the interrogative. Answer window stops at the first full stop: cut the elaboration 'nam mihi hoc erat, quod nunc est, Menaechmo: illum tum vocabant Sosiclem' which follows.

pairs.question: Quid erat nomen nostrae matri?
pairs.derivation: Menaechmus asks his newly-found twin the name of their mother; Sosicles answers with the name 'Teuximarchae'. Dropped speaker labels MEN./SOS. and the following 'MEN. Convenit' and inline verse number 1131.
